newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan power utilities to buy more electricity.
newsitem.headline: Japan power utilities to buy more electricity.

text.p: Japanese power utilities are due to step up wholesale purchases of electricity by issuing tenders to buy about 2.75 million kilowatts (kw) of power during fiscal 1997/98, an industry spokesman said on Thursday.

This is larger than the total volume of tenders issued by six power utilities during the current year to March 31, which amounted to 2.65 million kw, a spokesman for the Federation of Electric Power Companies said.
The figure for next fiscal year could increase if other companies, apart from the seven which have so far issued tenders, decide to follow suit.
Japan has 10 major power utility companies.
Japan's wholesale electricity business was liberalised just over a year ago to allow non-utilities to sell electricity on a wholesale basis to power companies.
The industry spokesman said several power utilities signed contracts to buy more electricity than the volume in their purchase tenders for the current fiscal year.
